fields.mechanism: Increase permeability through induced micro‑fractures (hydraulic fracturing) to accommodate fluid viscosity variations.
fields.intervention: Embed pressure‑activated micro‑fracture channels in the drainage floor that open under higher hydraulic pressure, dynamically adjusting flow pathways as water viscosity changes.
fields.expected_effect: Preserves the design flow rate across a wide viscosity range by providing additional flow paths when viscosity rises, eliminating hydraulic performance deviation.
fields.falsification_test: Run controlled bench tests with fluids of varying viscosity (e.g., water‑glycerol mixtures); measure flow rate through the modified floor versus a standard floor; validation occurs if flow stays within design limits for all viscosities.

fields.mechanism: Pore‑fracture structure provides passive hydraulic pathways that modulate flow resistance.
fields.intervention: Integrate a pre‑engineered micro‑fracture lattice into the drainage floor surface, creating a passive network of channels that open under hydraulic pressure to compensate for viscosity‑induced resistance.
fields.expected_effect: The passive micro‑fracture network maintains the design flow rate across the full viscosity range, reducing the hydraulic performance deviation.
fields.falsification_test: Perform flow‑rate measurements on a prototype floor with the micro‑fracture lattice while varying water viscosity (e.g., by adding glycerol); compare the deviation to a baseline floor without the lattice—if deviation is statistically insignificant, the mechanism is validated.

fields.mechanism: Hydraulic fracturing-induced fracture propagation that increases permeability of the medium.
fields.intervention: Implement localized high‑pressure fluid injection ports within the drainage floor to create controlled micro‑fractures, thereby dynamically adjusting the floor’s pore network in response to water viscosity changes.
fields.expected_effect: The induced micro‑fractures raise the effective permeability, compensating for higher viscosity and preserving the target flow rate across the viscosity range.

fields.mechanism: Hydraulic fracturing increases permeability of the medium, allowing flow to be maintained despite changes in fluid viscosity.
fields.intervention: Integrate a controlled micro‑fracturing/compliant porous layer within the drainage floor that opens under hydraulic pressure to create additional flow paths, mimicking hydraulic fracturing.
fields.expected_effect: The drainage floor will sustain the design flow rate across a range of water viscosities because the induced fractures reduce hydraulic resistance.
fields.falsification_test: Build a prototype floor with the micro‑fracture layer, run water of varying viscosities (e.g., pure water, glycerol‑water mixes), measure flow rates, and verify that rates stay within design limits; a failure to maintain flow disproves the mechanism.
